description: Analyze AI opportunity interview notes: screen tools, knowledge, skills and workflows; score impact and effort. Returns a draft record and report plan for host review, not files.

input.description: Interview notes or a full transcript, the business description, any earlier mini answers, an optional prior assessment record with its verification_needed list (JSON) and the requested scope, in the respondent's words with speaker labels. Send only information needed for this assessment; omit sensitive personal identifiers. Full assessment uses 16:9 slides. HOST REVIEW (static; each reply's host_review points here): Unreviewed draft. Compare every finding, quote and number with the current source; correct unsupported claims. metadata.client is the business name exactly as supplied, or Unknown when the source gives only a description. Add an opportunity for any task, repeated question, missing information, knowledge one person holds or wish in the source that the draft missed or folded into another, and merge opportunities that repeat one bottleneck. Recheck each impact and effort score, its quadrant and the matrix (a score of 7 or more is high: quick_wins is high impact with low effort, major_projects both high, fill_ins both low, thankless_tasks low impact with high effort, unscored when either score is unscored); move any record section (such as knowledge_domains, matrix, calculations, plan, discovery_gaps or skill_briefs) found outside record, or nested in another record section such as discovery, to the record's top level, and delete any key the item shapes do not list (such as analysis_only_reason). A task with no stated volume, consequence or process detail stays unscored. Preserve manual controls. Recheck each trial prerequisite: data permission is Not applicable unless customer details go into an AI tool (drafting for a particular customer from their message, invoice or record does), and a quote about approving output before it goes out is never prerequisite evidence. Remove any such quote; data permission then follows the rule just given, and trial approval is Unknown unless other evidence settles it. Keep every other prerequisite. A prerequisite marked Established or Not established without an exact source span becomes Unknown. Use only the values each field allows: prerequisite status Unknown, Established, Not established or Not applicable (Not applicable for data permission as above, for the baseline when the client does not do the task today, or for every prerequisite of an analysis-only item that changes nothing); opportunity status provisional, ready, blocked or deferred (analysis_only is a report_plan list, never a status: replace it with provisional); screen decision applicable, unnecessary or insufficient_evidence; knowledge modality systems, files, communications, spreadsheets, tacit or unknown. report_plan.recommended_choices holds recommendations for choices the source leaves open, not findings: keep each one, including the owner's approval. A recommended choice is never an opportunity: delete any opportunity that only restates one, such as an approval step for what goes out, from the record, matrix and report_plan. Every opportunity sits once across wins (at most four), later (at most three) and analysis_only (each analysis_only item an object with id and reason), and an item a client tool already handles is analysis_only. The helper is one role other than the owner (when the source names no one, propose one, such as a part-time assistant or student intern; never Unknown), with weekly hours the source states or To confirm. Drop any discovery gap that asks about a recommended choice. Each win gets a plan step that prepares on made-up inputs, and each win or later item whose types include skills has a skill brief with opportunity_id, name, trigger, inputs, decision_rules, output, and human_review; each verification claim states the fact to check. Strip any label, ID or comment from the quotes in calculations.assumptions. A verification_needed item the input already supplies as verified keeps its status, source_url and verified_on exactly as supplied. Check each other item on an official source and set status verified with its URL and date, or keep status unverified with its cost excluded. When report_plan is present, write the report deck and implementation guide copy yourself from the reviewed record and report_plan, following HOST REPORT COPY in the input parameter description; fill tool prices only from vendor pages checked today, compute any savings example yourself only from a quoted time for one task and a quoted weekly count (a weekly total such as two hours a week is not a time for one task) and recompute the cost subtotal. Ask the user for the client's logo; never invent one. Render with the pinned branding and layout in the input parameter description; verify asset hashes and run the self-inspection checklist on every page. Claim only actual downloads. Disclose corrections separately. STATIC HOST RENDERING SPECIFICATION. wins: one per report_plan.wins ID in order {id, pain 70: the problem today, fix 110: the concrete result, tool 18: the solution's name, use 72: what it does, following any recommended choice, cost 16: such as $20/mo, Free, Included or To confirm, setup 16: such as 1 hour, saves: the owner's hours back a week as a number, or Measure first, or New capacity}; later: one per report_plan.later ID {id, text 70: what it makes possible, tool 40}; analysis_only: report_plan.analysis_only unchanged; plan: exactly 4 days when there is a win, none otherwise {task 130: a plain action naming who does it, tool 30: the tool used that day, opportunity_ids: wins only}; costs {checked: the date you read the vendor pages, YYYY-MM-DD; rows: up to 7 {item 70, kind tool (a new tool) or other (another new monthly cost the plan adds, such as the helper's pay; leave out what the client already pays), month: USD from the vendor page or To confirm, year: USD for an annual plan, otherwise twelve months, source_url: the vendor page}}; hourly_value: what one hour of the owner's time is worth in USD, only as the client stated it, otherwise null; financial {roi_cap 90, time_cap 90, cost_cap 90: one caption under each figure, such as its basis, the price-check date or what is still to confirm}; next_steps: exactly 2 {heading 40, detail 200}: first, start Day One with the implementation guide; second, what to count for four weeks before the review call}. guide {roles: 2-4 {who 40, does 160}; rollout: 2-6 rows in time order {when 30, set_up 160, who 40}; steps: an optional setup-only first step (empty id and outcome) when accounts must be set up first, then one per win in order repeating its id, its tool as the title and its fix as the outcome {id, title 40, outcome 140, when 40, setup: 1-6 of 160, routine_label 30, routine: 0-5 of 160, working_when 140}; skills: one per record.skill_briefs item with the same name {name 30, build_in 30, connects_to 80, instructions 600}}. Limits are maxima, not targets. Writing rules: plain words a busy owner reads in one pass, short sentences, you for the owner, everyday verbs; no hype words, dashes for rhythm or recap lines. Each fix is a concrete thing that now exists or happens; never save time, spend less time or reduce alone. Use report_plan.helper's name everywhere, and for a proposed role write your plus the role in lower case (your part-time assistant); never a helper or the team. Recommend instead of asking: state each report_plan.recommended_choices choice in the win's use, pick one option with a reason for anything still open, and never hand a choice back, list decisions or offer two options for one job. Undecided review of what goes out means the owner approves each item on the phone before it goes out; it is never a prerequisite or a plan day. Name the tools the client already has; a new tool is a category plus the features that matter, never AI tool; drafting uses the client's AI assistant. Each new tool gets a kind tool cost row priced from the vendor page checked today with its URL, at nonprofit or discount pricing where the client qualifies, or To confirm and left out of the total; a dollar amount on a solution card repeats its row's price. Saves: a number only from a savings example you compute when calculations.assumptions quotes, word for word from the source, both the time one task takes and how many happen a week (a weekly total such as two hours a week is not a per-task time) (net = count x (before - after - extra review) - upkeep, after and upkeep labelled assumptions; a negative net is added work, never a saving), otherwise Measure first; work not done today is New capacity, never hours back; never count the helper's hours. Figures: weekly time returned is the sum of the numeric saves (Measure first when none); total monthly tool cost is the sum of the priced kind tool rows ($0 with no new tool, To confirm when none is priced); monthly net ROI = weekly time returned x 52 / 12 x hourly_value - the sum of every row's month, shown only when hourly_value is set, the time is a number and every row is priced, otherwise Measure first; never estimate an hourly value. time_cap says four weeks of tracking will confirm the hours. Plan: plain actions with an owner; with fewer than four, add in order: sign up for the new tool (the helper), make the first example together (the owner and the helper), agree the weekly review time (the owner). Open trial prerequisites from the record become plan days in plain words (time the task, confirm data permission), never a client decision. Trial gate: no step uses customer details before data_processing_permission is Established; a routine that uses AI on live work starts only after the owner approves the trial. Guide: addressed to you; setup steps start with a verb and name who does them; roles describe each part once the plan runs; skill instructions come from the brief's inputs, decision rules and human review, add no facts, mark unsure items [CHECK] (at least one), end with the owner's review and never send or publish on their own. Knowledge in the owner's head: one-press voice notes of the owner alone, sent to the person who drafts. Keep IDs, quotes, evidence, research, legal detail, risk lectures and rules the client already knows out of the copy, and costs and hours out of the guide; unknowns say To confirm. Before rendering, check that every record opportunity appears once across wins, later and analysis_only, guide steps repeat the wins' tools and fixes, every priced row has a vendor URL and check date, and the three figures recompute. Limits are maxima, not targets. Writing rules: plain words a busy owner reads in one pass, short sentences, you for the owner, everyday verbs; no hype words, dashes for rhythm or recap lines. Each fix is a concrete thing that now exists or happens; never save time, spend less time or reduce alone. Use report_plan.helper's name everywhere, and for a proposed role write your plus the role in lower case (your part-time assistant); never a helper or the team. Recommend instead of asking: state each report_plan.recommended_choices choice in the win's use, pick one option with a reason for anything still open, and never hand a choice back, list decisions or offer two options for one job. Undecided review of what goes out means the owner approves each item on the phone before it goes out; it is never a prerequisite or a plan day. Name the tools the client already has; a new tool is a category plus the features that matter, never AI tool; drafting uses the client's AI assistant. Each new tool gets a kind tool cost row priced from the vendor page checked today with its URL, at nonprofit or discount pricing where the client qualifies, or To confirm and left out of the total; a dollar amount on a solution card repeats its row's price. Saves: a number only from a savings example you compute when calculations.assumptions quotes, word for word from the source, both the time one task takes and how many happen a week (a weekly total such as two hours a week is not a per-task time) (net = count x (before - after - extra review) - upkeep, after and upkeep labelled assumptions; a negative net is added work, never a saving), otherwise Measure first; work not done today is New capacity, never hours back; never count the helper's hours. Figures: weekly time returned is the sum of the numeric saves (Measure first when none); total monthly tool cost is the sum of the priced kind tool rows ($0 with no new tool, To confirm when none is priced); monthly net ROI = weekly time returned x 52 / 12 x hourly_value - the sum of every row's month, shown only when hourly_value is set, the time is a number and every row is priced, otherwise Measure first; never estimate an hourly value. time_cap says four weeks of tracking will confirm the hours. Plan: plain actions with an owner; with fewer than four, add in order: sign up for the new tool (the helper), make the first example together (the owner and the helper), agree the weekly review time (the owner). Open trial prerequisites from the record become plan days in plain words (time the task, confirm data permission), never a client decision. Trial gate: no step uses customer details before data_processing_permission is Established; a routine that uses AI on live work starts only after the owner approves the trial. Guide: addressed to you; setup steps start with a verb and name who does them; roles describe each part once the plan runs; skill instructions come from the brief's inputs, decision rules and human review, add no facts, mark unsure items [CHECK] (at least one), end with the owner's review and never send or publish on their own. Knowledge in the owner's head: one-press voice notes of the owner alone, sent to the person who drafts. Keep IDs, quotes, evidence, research, legal detail, risk lectures and rules the client already knows out of the copy, and costs and hours out of the guide; unknowns say To confirm. handoff_brief.description: An object. Implementation brief. Scope handoff only: fill every field. For every other scope omit the whole object.

delivery_states.description: An object. evidenced only when the source supplies evidence.

selected_ids.description: A list. Opportunity IDs that exist in record.opportunities.

separately_scoped.description: A list. Work that needs its own scope; no offers, prices or bookings.

instruction.description: Text. Copy the expected value character for character; never shorten or reword it. Expected value: "Unreviewed draft. Before writing or rendering anything, follow HOST REVIEW in this tool's input parameter description.".

required.description: true or false. Expected value: true.

record.description: An object. Assessment record, schema 1.0.0. Only IDs, scores, quadrants, each opportunity's trial_prerequisites statuses, the matrix and savings arithmetic are required, so a long reply is not rejected; still fill every key the method calls for, including trial_prerequisites evidence, evidence_ids and discovery_gaps. Out-of-scope sections keep pasted values or stay empty. The record closes only after workflow_briefs: matrix, calculations, plan and discovery_gaps sit inside it, never at the top level.

assumptions.description: A list. Each item is one source sentence that states how long one task takes or how many happen a week, copied word for word inside single quotes with no label, ID or comment, for example 'Each reminder takes me roughly 6 minutes to write'. Empty when the source states neither.

basis.description: Text. Always exactly measure_first from this tool. One of: "illustrative", "estimate", "measured", "measure_first".

net_minutes_per_week.description: Text. Always exactly Measure first from this tool.

rows.description: A list. Always an empty list from this tool. The host computes any savings example.

actor.description: Text. Whose minutes: owner, employee, team or Unknown. Never add person totals to team totals.

after_minutes.description: A number. Minutes per task after, covering the same steps as before including retained review; labelled assumption unless measured.

before_minutes.description: A number. Minutes per task before, as stated in the source (never derived from a weekly total); same steps as after.

benefit_group.description: Text. One distinct benefit group per row.

extra_review_minutes.description: A number. Added review minutes per task not already in after.

volume_per_week.description: A number. Tasks per week from the source.

upkeep_minutes_per_week.description: Text. Always exactly Unknown from this tool.

discovery.description: An object. Only these six keys; discovery_gaps is a record key after plan. Name people by role, never he or she unless the source says.

quantity.description: Text. As stated with its unit, or Unknown.

question.description: Text. One focused question, never about a choice report_plan.recommended_choices makes.

derivation.description: Text. derivation: the arithmetic or inference and the statement IDs it uses. statement: empty.

id.description: Text. E1, E2 ... stable across calls.

location.description: Text. Supplied line, timestamp or section, or Not supplied.

quote.description: Text. statement: exact contiguous source text. derivation: empty.

speaker.description: Text. Supplied speaker label, or Supplied context. When the notes warn that labels may be wrong, a first-person answer to the interviewer's question is the respondent's. Empty for derivation.

conflict_resolution.description: Text. Which source wins and who decides when sources disagree, or Unknown.

opportunity_ids.description: A list. Opportunity IDs that exist in record.opportunities.

priority_question.description: Text. The business question this knowledge answers.

proposed_home.description: Text. Proposed canonical home for this knowledge, or Unknown. A proposal, not a provisioned location.

refresh_cadence.description: Text. Proposed refresh cadence, or Unknown.

fill_ins.description: A list. Scored opportunity IDs that exist in record.opportunities; never an unscored one. Each ID sits in the list named by its own quadrant field; an unscored opportunity sits only in unscored, even when it is a win.

major_projects.description: A list. Scored opportunity IDs that exist in record.opportunities; never an unscored one. Each ID sits in the list named by its own quadrant field; an unscored opportunity sits only in unscored, even when it is a win.

evidence.description: Text. Verbatim source span about whether the task's data is complete and usable, or an empty string.

reason.description: Text. At most 350 characters. Why it is not a win or later item: a hard constraint, already handled by a tool the client uses, overlapping another opportunity, too little evidence of the task, or ranked below the chosen items. When the source says a tool the client already uses does this, the reason is that it is already handled by that tool. An open prerequisite is not a reason.

bottleneck.description: Text. The bottleneck in plain words, one short sentence.

place.description: Text. Expected value: one of "win", "later", "analysis_only". The report_plan list that holds this ID. Never an opportunity status.

helper.description: An object. The one person other than the owner who does the legwork.

weekly_hours.description: Text. At most 30 characters. That person's hours as the source states them, or To confirm. Never computed from task times.

who.description: Text. At most 40 characters. One role other than the owner: as supplied, or when the source names no one, a proposed role such as a part-time assistant or student intern. Never the owner and never two options.

later.description: A list. 0-3 opportunity IDs that come after the wins, never every supported opportunity. Never an item that changes nothing: a task a client tool already handles is analysis_only.

recommended_choices.description: A list. 0-3 recommendations that replace choices the source leaves open, each one line naming the item, for example The owner approves each post on the phone before it goes out. Never a question, two options or a choice the source already made.

skill_brief_ids.description: A list. The wins and later IDs whose types include skills, in that order. record.skill_briefs holds exactly one brief per listed ID.

wins.description: A list. 0-4 opportunity IDs, best first. At least one when any opportunity is supported by the evidence; unscored, provisional and blocked opportunities can be wins.

verification_needed.description: A list. Every current tool capability, plan or price claim. The host verifies or keeps it provisional.

check.description: Text. What to confirm on an official source.

claim.description: Text. The capability, plan or price fact to check, in plain words, about a tool the input names or the change recommends. Never a rule or instruction.

roi_effect.description: Text. What stays excluded or provisional until verified.

source_url.description: Text. Official source URL the host checked, or empty. Carry over unchanged from a pasted record.

status.description: Text. unverified when returned by this tool; the host sets verified or contradicted after checking. Carry over unchanged from a pasted record. One of: "unverified", "verified", "contradicted".

verified_on.description: Text. Check date YYYY-MM-DD, or empty. Carry over unchanged from a pasted record.
